prompt.title: Online learning for school students
prompt.text:
Some people believe that school students learn better online than in a traditional classroom. Others think face-to-face lessons are more effective.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Use reasons and relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

You should write at least 250 words.

essay:
The rapid spread of digital technology has prompted a heated debate about whether school students are better served by online learning or by conventional classroom teaching. Although virtual lessons offer undeniable flexibility, I would argue that face-to-face instruction remains more effective for most pupils.

Advocates of online education point to its convenience and personalisation. Learners can progress at their own pace, replay explanations they found difficult and access high-quality materials regardless of where they live. A teenager in a remote province, for instance, may be able to follow a physics course delivered by an outstanding teacher in Hanoi, an opportunity that would otherwise be out of reach. Furthermore, adaptive learning platforms can identify each student's weaknesses and recommend targeted exercises, something a single teacher with forty pupils can rarely do.

Nevertheless, there are compelling reasons to believe that the physical classroom is irreplaceable. Firstly, children and adolescents generally lack the self-discipline required to study alone in front of a screen, where social media and games are only a click away. During the pandemic, many schools reported a sharp decline in attendance and motivation once lessons moved online. Secondly, learning is a social process: by debating ideas, collaborating on projects and receiving immediate feedback, students develop communication skills and emotional maturity that no video call can fully replicate. Finally, online learning risks widening the gap between rich and poor families, since not every household can afford a reliable device and internet connection.

In conclusion, while online learning is a valuable supplement, particularly for revision and for students in isolated areas, it should not replace traditional schooling. The most sensible approach is a blended model in which teachers remain at the heart of education and technology is used to enhance, rather than substitute, their work.
